clue.text: Dicky, Sue, and Sam are to take over

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the names that follow are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people, Sue and Sam, are stepping in to replace someone whose own position looks shaky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a third name in the list, but it is the anagram signal: SUESAM rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a role or duty is to take it on, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Run out for a lighter

definitions.meaning: to overflow or slop out, as liquid from a full cup
a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire or pipe

explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that runs out of a vessel has slopped over; a taper of twisted paper for kindling also bears the name.

clue.text: A French Communist backing the worker in secret

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for a Communist is reversed

parts.note: a red is a Communist
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A French Communist secretly supports a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like 'supporting', but it reverses RED to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand means done deceitfully or slyly, out of sight, so in secret.

clue.text: City money raised for confectionery

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted upwards, so the currency word reads bottom to top

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries

explanation.surface: Money from the City has been put up to pay for sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses RIAL to LAIR in this down entry; EC is the postal district of London's financial City.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a cream-filled pastry, an item of sweet confectionery.

clue.text: Calling for transport in Eastern ship

parts.note: a bus is a means of public transport
taken as written
E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone describes their vocation as running transport aboard a ship in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but here it simply supplies its own letters in the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a trade or occupation, and business is a line of work, a synonym.

clue.text: He was an arresting man

parts.note: reads as a striking, eye-catching fellow, but means an officer who made arrests

explanation.walkthrough: These were London's first professional police, attached to the magistrates' court in a street in Covent Garden in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this early London police force caught criminals, so made arrests.

clue.text: Well, the queen shows such a dog

parts.note: a spring is a natural well or source of water
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen shows off a particular breed of dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like an interjection opening the sentence, but it gives SPRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer spaniel is a breed of gundog.

clue.text: Musical composition — there's no catch in this clue!

parts.note: taken as written
a net is used to catch fish

explanation.surface: A piece of music is offered, with the reassurance that this clue has no trick in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no catch' looks like 'no trick', but reads literally as NO NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a piece written for nine performers.

clue.text: Is tried as ordered, and subjected to scorn

indicators.note: ordered means put into order, so the letters of the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is put on trial as instructed and then mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like 'commanded', but rearranges ISTRIEDAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be satirised is to be mocked or ridiculed, held up to scorn.

clue.text: Wood-anemone found in bend by river?

parts.note: to wind is to bend or twist in a curve
in crosswords a river is a 'flower', something that flows

explanation.surface: A woodland plant is spotted growing at a bend of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the crossword joke that a river is a 'flower', one that flows; 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood anemone is a spring plant also known by the common name of windflower.

clue.text: A sound record

definitions.meaning: a single musical tone or noise
to write something down briefly, as in jotting a memo

explanation.definitionFit: A musical tone is a note, and to note something is to record it in writing.

clue.text: Scaremonger gets weapon shown in a catalogue

indicators.note: shown in says the weapon word appears placed inside the phrase for a catalogue

parts.note: a list is a catalogue of items
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A fearmonger acquires a gun that appears in a sales catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown in' is the container signal; 'a' is kept as a letter in its own right, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaremonger spreads needless fear, which is exactly what an alarmist does.

clue.text: "Accuse not —, she hath done her part." (Milton)

definitions.text: "Accuse not —, she hath done her part." (Milton)

parts.words: "Accuse not —, she hath done her part." (Milton)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Paradise Lost, where the missing word is the force personified as a woman who has done her share in creating Eve

explanation.surface: A line of Milton's verse with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Paradise Lost, Book VIII: the angel Raphael tells Adam not to blame the natural world for his weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: In the quoted line the natural world, personified as female, is the one Adam is told not to blame.

clue.text: Prima-donna keen to make a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means returning, so the word for keen is read from back to front

parts.note: avid means keen or eager

explanation.surface: An opera star is eager to return to the stage after time away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a comeback' reverses AVID.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is the leading female opera singer, and diva is the usual synonym.

clue.text: It's rough for the partisan

definitions.meaning: a guerrilla fighter outside the regular army

explanation.definitionFit: Uneven ground is not smooth; a guerrilla fighter is also a soldier outside official forces.

clue.text: Training cut without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for cut wraps around the hesitation sound

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A training session is cut short with no dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means 'lacking', but here it carries its old sense of 'outside', so the cut goes around the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise is physical training, a synonym.

clue.text: Ganymede's saucer

parts.note: reads as a piece of crockery, but a saucer is literally a thing that carries a cup, which was Ganymede's role for the gods

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Ganymede was the youth carried off by Zeus to serve wine to the gods on Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede poured wine for the gods, holding their drinking vessel, just as a saucer holds a cup.

clue.text: Fellow with a sound job in some craft

definitions.text: Fellow with a sound job in some craft

parts.words: Fellow with a sound job in some craft
parts.note: reads as a secure job in a trade, but means a sailor on a boat who sounds the depth of water with a weighted line

explanation.definitionFit: A seaman who measures water depth by dropping a weighted line is said to sound it.

clue.text: An inclination for treading in a mess

indicators.note: in a mess means jumbled up, so the letters of the word before are disordered

explanation.surface: A slope is treacherous to walk on when it is in a muddy state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' rearranges TREADING.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, and an inclination is a slope or incline.

clue.text: Guards step around hundreds

indicators.note: around tells us the word for a step is placed outside the numeral

parts.note: a pas is a step in dancing, from French
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, so a number of hundreds

explanation.surface: Sentries pace around in their hundreds.
explanation.walkthrough: PAS, the ballet term for a step, goes around D, the Roman five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Pads are protective guards, like the leg pads worn in cricket.

clue.text: Sailor Bill goes to America for the summer

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
AC is short for account, a bill
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A sailor named Bill heads to America for the summer season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like the sailor's name; 'summer' means one who sums, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A counting frame with beads is used to add up numbers, so it is a device that sums.

clue.text: A key in gold — quite ancient

indicators.note: in places the musical key inside the word for gold

parts.note: taken as written
E is one of the musical keys, A to G

explanation.surface: A key made of gold turns out to be very old.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then E inside GOLD. Keys A to G are a crossword stock for single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something age-old has existed for a very long time, so it is very old indeed.

clue.text: Starts giving some help to pensioners

indicators.note: some means only a part of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: A new service begins by offering a little help to retired people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks letters from 'help to pensioners'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that opens begins or gets going, so it starts.

clue.text: It may be held up in bad weather

definitions.text: It may be held up in bad weather

parts.words: It may be held up in bad weather
parts.note: reads like a delayed train or flight, but means an object raised over the head when it rains

explanation.definitionFit: A rain cover on a stick is raised overhead in wet weather to keep you dry.

clue.text: Left only a little land? That's a yarn!

parts.note: an isle is a small island, a little bit of land

explanation.surface: Someone claims they were left only a scrap of land, and the listener scoffs at the tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a tall story but means thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread, a kind of yarn used for stockings.

clue.text: Spend unwisely, being depressed

definitions.meaning: British slang for squandering money, as in to throw it away

explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for squandering cash (often spelt blew/blow); it is also the usual colour word for feeling sad.

clue.text: She expects to be offered a hand when at work

definitions.text: She expects to be offered a hand when at work

parts.words: She expects to be offered a hand when at work
parts.note: reads as someone wanting help or applause on the job, but means a beautician whose client literally holds out a hand to be groomed

explanation.definitionFit: A nail technician tends clients' fingernails, so each customer extends a hand for treatment.

clue.text: A restrained person

parts.note: reads as someone calm and self-controlled, but means someone physically held captive

explanation.definitionFit: A captive in jail is literally held under restraint.

clue.text: Shield made of hide

definitions.meaning: a protective barrier, as a verb or noun

explanation.definitionFit: A partition protects or shields, and to conceal something behind one is to hide it.
